extracted.intended_audience: Independent OPOs (IOPOs), histocompatibility laboratories (HCLs), transplant hospitals (THs), Medicare contractors, and OPO industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Medicare regulatory requirements and policies for establishing interim organ acquisition rates (SACs), reconciling organ acquisition costs, and determining allowable organ procurement and testing costs for IOPOs and HCLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor-established interim rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim rates are contractor established rates, based on costs associated with procuring an organ for transplantation, incurred by an IOPO or HCL during its previous fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed revision of §413.420(d)(2) and addition of (d)(2)(i) and (ii) specify contractor establishes interim rates. If there is not adequate cost data to determine the initial interim rate, the contractor would determine it according to the IOPO's or HCL's estimate of its projected costs for the fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor establishes non-renal organ-specific SACs
rubrics_metrics.description: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027, the interim rates for non-renal organs are contractor established non-renal organ-specific SACs or contractor established rates, based on costs associated with procuring each specific type of non-renal organ for transplantation, incurred by an IOPO or HCL during its previous fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor to establish, adjust (if necessary), and publish non-renal interim rates using the same procedures used for establishing kidney SACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of interim rates
rubrics_metrics.description: When a contractor establishes interim rates for IOPOs and HCLs, it must disseminate those interim rates to all THs, OPOs, and contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed change to §413.420(d)(4) adds OPOs to list of recipients; ensures transparency since OPOs also pay IOPOs for organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation of interim-rate payments with IOPO/HCL
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments or amounts payable from THs and OPOs based on interim rates are reconciled directly with the IOPO or HCL after the close of its fiscal year in accordance with §413.420(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §413.420(d)(3) clarifies that reconciliation applies to interim rates as proposed in (d)(2)(i) and (ii) and will follow §413.420(e) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive adjustment on accrual basis
rubrics_metrics.description: A retroactive adjustment of the amounts received or receivable by the IOPO or HCL under the interim rates is made in accordance with §413.64(f) and reflects the accrual basis of accounting required at §413.24(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed revisions explicitly add 'received or receivable' language to reflect accrual accounting; applies to kidney and proposed non-renal interim rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lump-sum adjustment for overpayment/underpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the determination of reasonable cost reveals an overpayment or underpayment resulting from interim reimbursement rates received or receivable by the IOPO or HCL from THs and OPOs, a lump sum adjustment is made directly between the contractor and the IOPO or HCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.420(e)(2)(ii) (kidney) and proposed §413.420(e)(3)(ii) (non-renal) specify lump sum adjustments; identifies both THs and OPOs as paying entities in reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor review of cost reports to set new interim rates
rubrics_metrics.description: For cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027, a cost report submitted by an IOPO or HCL is reviewed by the contractor and new interim reimbursement rates for non-renal organ acquisition costs for the subsequent fiscal year are established by the contractor based upon this review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.420(e)(3) parallels existing kidney language and links cost report review directly to contractor-established interim rates for following year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ-specific SAC calculation — per-organ rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For each organ type, the contractor establishes the organ-specific SAC based on an estimate of initial year projected or subsequent years' actual, reasonable and necessary costs the IOPO expects to incur to procure deceased donor organs during the IOPO's cost reporting period, divided by the initial year projected or subsequent years' actual, number of usable deceased donor organs the IOPO expects to procure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled after existing kidney SAC regulations at §413.404(c)(2)(i); proposed §413.404(d)(1) adds 'For each organ type' and replaces kidney-specific language with organ-specific language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-year SAC based on IOPO budget information
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor develops the IOPO's initial organ-specific SAC based on the IOPO's budget information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.404(d)(1)(i) models after existing regulation text for kidney initial SACs at §413.404(c)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent-year SAC based on prior-year actuals
rubrics_metrics.description: For each organ type, the contractor computes the organ-specific SAC for subsequent years using the IOPO's costs related to organ acquisition that were incurred in the prior cost reporting period and dividing those costs by the number of usable deceased donor organs procured during that cost reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.404(d)(1)(ii) models after §413.404(c)(2)(iii) kidney rules; ties subsequent SAC to prior period actuals and usable organ counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ-specific SAC equals interim payment amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Each organ-specific SAC amount is the organ-specific interim payment the TH or other OPO pays to the IOPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.404(d)(1)(iii) explicitly states equivalence between organ-specific SAC and organ-specific interim payment as set forth in §413.420(d)(2)(i) and (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable organ acquisition cost categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs that may be used to develop IOPO deceased donor SACs include, but are not limited to: costs of organs acquired from other THs or OPOs; transportation costs as specified in §413.402(b)(8); surgeons' fees for excising deceased donor organs (limited to $1,250 for kidneys); tissue typing services (including independent labs); organ preservation and perfusion costs; general routine and special care service costs (e.g., ICU/CCU services related to donor); operating room and other inpatient ancillary service costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.404(d)(1)(iv) adopts the listing used in §413.404(b)(3)(ii)(C) for transplant hospital deceased donor SACs, except it excludes registry fees (costs incurred by THs not OPOs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of registry fees from IOPO SAC cost listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Registry fees are excluded from the listing of organ acquisition costs IOPOs should use when developing deceased donor SACs because registry fees are costs incurred by transplant hospitals, not OPOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies difference between TH and IOPO allowable cost items; carried through proposed §413.404(d)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only contractor may adjust organ SACs
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the contractor may adjust the organ SACs. IOPOs may request that the contractor make an adjustment in accordance with §413.64(e), or the contractor may initiate an adjustment in accordance with §413.64(d)(2) or §413.64(e) as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.404(d)(1)(v) changes existing policy where IOPOs could adjust their non-renal SACs without contractor approval; intent is to centralize adjustment authority with contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-IOPO organ transfer billing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IOPO obtains an organ from another IOPO, the receiving IOPO is responsible for paying the procuring IOPO's SAC; the receiving IOPO uses its SAC for each organ type, and not the procuring IOPO's SAC, when billing the TH receiving the organ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §413.404(d)(2) continues existing policy at §413.404(c)(3) without change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor review of MCRs to determine Medicare share and reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: To reconcile Medicare's share of non-renal organ acquisition costs, the contractor would review the MCR to determine if the costs are reasonable, ensuring that IOPO and HCL organ acquisition costs reported on MCRs are allowable and are reasonable and necessary in accordance with section 1861(v) of the Act, the regulations, and PRM-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed policy entails contractor's review of all IOPO and HCL organ acquisition costs reported annually; if finalized, CMS would update the IOPO and HCL cost report CMS-216-94 to enable reconciliation by organ type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption about beneficiary attribution for reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconciliation assumes that all usable organs or tests for usable organs intended for transplant are for Medicare beneficiaries, except for usable organs or tests sent to military hospitals, VA hospitals, or foreign countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption mirrors the current approach used for kidney reconciliation and is proposed to apply to non-renal organ reconciliation as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of perfusion and attempted-procurement costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred for organs intended for transplant, including costly interventions such as perfusion, are allowable even if the organ is subsequently not transplanted; perfusion costs are allowed per §413.402(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IOPO authorized perfusion of a non-renal organ intended for transplant that was subsequently not transplanted, those costs would be allowable; if a TH authorized perfusion, the perfusion costs belong to that TH and should be billed directly to the TH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable cost principles / Medicare statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare reimburses providers for actual costs incurred for Medicare-related items and services, excluding unnecessary costs, based on section 1861(v) of the Act and regulations under 42 CFR part 413 and PRM-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers reimbursed on reasonable cost basis (including OPOs and HCLs) must follow part 413 rules; Secretary authorized to define reasonable costs; amounts paid must not exceed costs incurred and must be determined per statutory/regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPOs subject to part 413 and reasonable cost rules
rubrics_metrics.description: OPOs are identified in §413.1(a)(2)(v) as a provider type to which part 413 applies and are expressly subject to Medicare's reasonable cost principles, including 42 CFR 413.9 regarding costs related to patient care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement rebuts assertions that OPOs are not subject to reasonable cost rules because they do not provide direct patient care; OPO organ acquisition costs arise under Medicare statute and are governed by section 1861(v) and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim payments, cost report settlement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare makes interim payments through claims processing (and for pass-through costs based on estimated costs or predetermined rates); after the cost reporting period, providers submit an MCR, the contractor reviews it, and calculates a settlement by comparing interim payments to actual allowable reasonable costs; overpayments must be repaid, underpayments paid to provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes cash flow mechanism and final settlement mechanics for providers reimbursed on reasonable cost basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudent buyer principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit in reasonable cost policy is that providers will seek to minimize costs — a prudent and cost-conscious buyer will not pay more than the going price and will seek discounts; costs exceeding what prudent buyers would incur are not allowable absent clear evidence the higher costs were unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRM-1 chapter 21, section 2103 examples: (1) buying from a higher-cost supplier without justification leads to exclusion of excess cost; (2) rental arrangements that indirectly discount supply costs must be reflected as cost reductions; (3) leasing equipment internally rather than competitive bidding that results in higher costs will be disallowed to the extent a prudent buyer would have paid less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reporting expectations for HCLs
rubrics_metrics.description: HCLs must provide complete and transparent MCR reporting (e.g., complete worksheet A-1 and clearly explain 'Other' amounts on worksheet A-3) because lack of transparency raises questions about payment accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS review found many HCLs missing worksheets or reporting large unexplained 'Other' costs; contractors will review MCR data for allowability and reasonableness; OIG audits found unallowable costs often due to inadequate documentation or improper allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timing, reporting form updates, and burden considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed one-year delay to implement changes (effective for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2027) to allow time to update IOPO and HCL cost report form CMS-216-94 and for providers to prepare for increased reporting and contractor oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects necessary data are already collected by IOPOs but acknowledges potential reporting burden; contractor administrative costs included in contract and offset by estimated Medicare savings beginning FY2028.
